label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 12 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 189.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was recreated at 18:39:02 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. At 18:39:04 the receiver queued evt_000270 (key pay_000248) to provider-events 2@86, and the ledger rejects it: 'amount must be positive integer cents'. With retry, the consumer keeps retrying that one message with backoff capped at 15 s and never moves past it. Lag grows on all three partitions, so the whole consumer is blocked, not just partition 2. The money check then times out waiting for the ledger to reach its cutoff, which is BooksBehindProvider. payment-confirmer, with dead_letter, dead-lettered the same message and has no lag.

evidence.shows: Ledger lag on partitions 0, 1 and 2 was 0 at 18:38:58 and rose steadily to 79, 98 and 88 at 18:40:18. Confirmer lag stays at 0 apart from one blip, so Kafka and the topic are healthy.

From 18:39:06 to 18:40:20 ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for source provider-events/2@86, with error 'amount must be positive integer cents', attempts 3 to 10 and retry_in_seconds capped at 15.
ledger-consumer was recreated at 18:39:02 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. Every other service dates from 18:37:36.

Trace of evt_000270: the producer sent it to partition 2 offset 86. Every ledger span is status error, outcome will_retry, with the amount error, about 75 s of retries in all. The confirmer span's outcome is dead_lettered.
The receiver logged 'webhook queued' for evt_000270, key pay_000248, partition 2, offset 86, at 18:39:04.569, two seconds after the ledger-consumer redeploy.
Lag summed per partition went from 0 to 72, 86 and 77 at 18:40:15, matching the alert.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the settings it ran before the 18:39:02 deploy, expected to be BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. The stuck message 2@86 should then be dead-lettered and the backlog drained. Afterwards: inspect evt_000270 in the dead-letter store, compare it with the provider's record of pay_000248, and book or correct it by hand. Then run the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, and the backlog grows a little more. The rollback may also revert LEDGER_HANDLER if the deploy changed it. evt_000270 will not be booked in the ledger, so the books will miss pay_000248 until someone repairs them by hand. If the earlier settings were also BAD_EVENTS=retry, the rollback will not unblock anything. Other malformed events further back would be dead-lettered too.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the 18:39:02 settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). Dead-lettered messages stay in the dead-letter store and can be replayed later. Nothing is lost from provider-events.
